$comment: Mission 1.84.12. The census of gate v1.3.0's deterministic semantic rules, the prompt block rendered from its first-class policy objects, and the checks that bind them. Nothing here reads an answer to render text; CI gate 79 re-derives every field.

RECONFIRMED_FROM_MERGED_ARTIFACTS.GATE_V1_3_0_REFUSED_STATEMENT: Transactions or tenders occur in the bounded scope of CPV class 9261 notices.

CENSUS.accepts: an answer the v1.1.0 schema validates
CENSUS.refuses: a missing, extra or out-of-bound field, reported by the v1.1.0 validator
v1_2_evidence: THE OUTPUT CONTRACT IS BOUNDED, AND AN ANSWER THAT EXCEEDS A BOUND IS REFUSED RATHER THAN TRIMMED.
CENSUS.rationale: the output-contract block v1.2.0 renders from the schema states every generation-relevant bound, so the schema needs no semantic prose

CENSUS.accepts: EXPLORATORY
CENSUS.refuses: any other value on a FORM_HYPOTHESIS answer
CENSUS.rationale: a closed choice of one, rendered by the contract and restated by v1.2.0

CENSUS.accepts: at least one item
CENSUS.refuses: an empty list on a FORM_HYPOTHESIS answer
CENSUS.rationale: the schema sets no minimum, and v1.2.0 says what the field names but not that it may not be empty
CENSUS.instruction: recommended_next_evidence has at least one item

CENSUS.accepts: at least one classified statement
CENSUS.refuses: an empty list on a FORM_HYPOTHESIS answer
CENSUS.rationale: the schema sets no minimum, and 'classify every substantive statement' does not say the list may not be empty
CENSUS.instruction: statement_classifications has at least one item

CENSUS.accepts: the three classification labels
CENSUS.refuses: any other label
v1_2_evidence: classification: exactly one of: OBSERVED_OR_EVIDENCE_SUPPORTED, HYPOTHESIS_TO_VALIDATE, UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE
CENSUS.rationale: a closed choice the contract renders member by member

CENSUS.accepts: at least one HYPOTHESIS_TO_VALIDATE or UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE item
CENSUS.refuses: a list in which every item is classified OBSERVED_OR_EVIDENCE_SUPPORTED
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 defines the three classifications and never says one of the other two is required
CENSUS.instruction: at least one item of statement_classifications is HYPOTHESIS_TO_VALIDATE or UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE: a packet this narrow always leaves something to test or something unknown

CENSUS.accepts: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, recorded as a correct outcome that creates no Opportunity
CENSUS.refuses: nothing: it ends the gate with no hypothesis formed
v1_2_evidence: DECIDE. If the packet supports a narrow hypothesis, answer FORM_HYPOTHESIS.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0's DECIDE paragraph states both answers and prefers the refusal to a hypothesis that needs an unsupplied fact

CENSUS.accepts: FORM_HYPOTHESIS or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
CENSUS.refuses: any other value
CENSUS.rationale: a closed choice the contract renders
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^decision .* is not one of the two permitted values

CENSUS.accepts: a packet whose every source has registry labels in the metadata channel
CENSUS.refuses: a packet source the caller declared no names for
CENSUS.rationale: the caller builds the metadata channel from the registry; no answer can satisfy or break it

CENSUS.accepts: the packet's subject label, exactly
CENSUS.refuses: any other subject
CENSUS.rationale: the task prints the SUBJECT and never says the field must carry it unchanged
CENSUS.instruction: subject is the SUBJECT the task names, copied exactly

CENSUS.accepts: Evidence ids the packet supplied
CENSUS.refuses: an Evidence id the packet does not carry
v1_2_evidence: the ids supplied to you, copied verbatim. No prose, no description, no partial id.
CENSUS.rationale: the contract's own note says to copy the supplied ids verbatim
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^cited Evidence ids not in the packet

CENSUS.accepts: Claim ids the packet supplied
CENSUS.refuses: a Claim id the packet does not carry
v1_2_evidence: the ids supplied to you, copied verbatim. No prose, no description, no partial id.
CENSUS.rationale: the contract's own note says to copy the supplied ids verbatim
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^cited Claim ids not in the packet

CENSUS.accepts: at least one cited Evidence id
CENSUS.refuses: no Evidence id cited
CENSUS.rationale: the schema sets no minimum, and v1.2.0 says which ids may be cited but not that one must be
CENSUS.instruction: supporting_evidence_ids cites at least one Evidence id

CENSUS.accepts: at least one cited Claim id
CENSUS.refuses: no Claim id cited
CENSUS.rationale: the schema sets no minimum, and v1.2.0 says which ids may be cited but not that one must be
CENSUS.instruction: supporting_claim_ids cites at least one Claim id

CENSUS.accepts: every cited Evidence id together with the Claim id it is labelled with
CENSUS.refuses: an Evidence id cited without its Claim
CENSUS.rationale: Evidence is claim-relative; the task labels each pair and never says the pair travels together
CENSUS.instruction: every Evidence id in supporting_evidence_ids has the Claim id it is labelled with in supporting_claim_ids

CENSUS.accepts: family names the packet supplied
CENSUS.refuses: a family the packet does not carry
v1_2_evidence: the family names supplied to you as a packet fact, copied verbatim.
CENSUS.rationale: the contract's own note says to copy the supplied family names verbatim
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^source families the packet does not carry

CENSUS.accepts: dimensions the packet carries
CENSUS.refuses: a dimension claimed as supported that the packet does not carry
v1_2_evidence: A dimension you were not given evidence for is UNSUPPORTED
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 says a dimension without evidence is unsupported, and the task lists the supported ones
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^dimensions claimed as supported that this packet does not carry

CENSUS.accepts: two disjoint lists
CENSUS.refuses: a dimension listed as both supported and unsupported
CENSUS.rationale: nothing in v1.2.0 says the two lists may not share a name
CENSUS.instruction: no dimension appears both in supported_dimensions and in unsupported_dimensions

CENSUS.accepts: every mandatory dimension the packet does not carry, listed as unsupported
CENSUS.refuses: a mandatory dimension left unmentioned
v1_2_evidence: dimensions you MUST report on and mark unsupported unless a supplied
CENSUS.rationale: the task names the dimensions that must be reported and marked unsupported

CENSUS.accepts: a restatement recording UNKNOWN
CENSUS.refuses: a status without UNKNOWN, or one calling the sources independent
v1_2_evidence: INDEPENDENCE AND RELIABILITY are supplied to you as facts about the packet.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 says to repeat the packet's independence fact as given and never to call source families independent sources

CENSUS.accepts: a restatement of the packet's scorability in the task's own terms
CENSUS.refuses: a status that drops the scorability the packet has
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 says to repeat the reliability fact as given, and the task gives it
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^(?:no row in this packet is scoring-eligible and reliability_status|\d+ of \d+ rows are scoring-eligible and reliability_status)

CENSUS.accepts: every text, each read in its field's context
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: it collects the findings the rules below produce
CENSUS.rationale: the aggregation that turns findings into refusals; the rules it aggregates are listed on their own

CENSUS.accepts: only the contract's fields
CENSUS.refuses: a field the field-context policy does not name
v1_2_evidence: every one required, and no other field.
CENSUS.rationale: the contract says the object carries no other field
CENSUS.refusal_signature: has no field context, so its text cannot be read as anything

CENSUS.accepts: an item carrying one of the three labels
CENSUS.refuses: an item whose label has no disposition
v1_2_evidence: classification: exactly one of: OBSERVED_OR_EVIDENCE_SUPPORTED, HYPOTHESIS_TO_VALIDATE, UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE
CENSUS.rationale: a closed choice the contract renders member by member

CENSUS.accepts: a definitional identifier a trusted fact carries
CENSUS.refuses: an identifier of a trusted scheme that no trusted fact supplies
CENSUS.rationale: an external definition is prior knowledge, which v1.2.0 says is unavailable
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^the definitional identifier \S+ is supplied by no trusted

CENSUS.accepts: a number a source content statement or a packet structural fact carries
CENSUS.refuses: any other number, including a figure that occurs only inside a source name
v1_2_evidence: NUMBERS. You may restate a number that appears in a supplied statement.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 states the rule for numbers; the source-name part is rendered with the metadata rule
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^the number \S+ appears in no source content statement

CENSUS.accepts: an uncertainty that states what is not known; a request that names what would have to be observed
CENSUS.refuses: an item that asserts instead, which is then read as the assertion it became
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 names what the fields are for and never says their text keeps that shape; rendered from the field policy at proposition level, without the patterns that read it

CENSUS.accepts: text that does what its field does
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: each field's disposition decides which rules read its text
CENSUS.rationale: which fields assert, which propose a test and which only name an unknown decides what a word may do in each; v1.2.0 never says so, and the field policy is its first-class source

CENSUS.accepts: a transformation concept denied, listed as not supported, or named as unknown
CENSUS.refuses: a transformation concept asserted with no source content statement asserting it
v1_2_evidence: WHAT THIS PACKET IS AND IS NOT. Each line is refused by a deterministic gate.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0's anti-distortion block states each transformation and what it is not

CENSUS.accepts: an added concept denied, listed as not supported, or named as unknown
CENSUS.refuses: an added concept asserted with no source content statement asserting it
CENSUS.rationale: gate v1.2.0 added concepts the v1.2.0 prompt never names; rendered from each concept's own name and never-text, and never from its phrases

CENSUS.accepts: a trusted identifier restated as the limit it is
CENSUS.refuses: a trusted identifier cited for the concept its fact limits
v1_2_evidence: WHAT THIS PACKET IS AND IS NOT. Each line is refused by a deterministic gate.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0's anti-distortion block pairs each definition with what it is not

CENSUS.accepts: a score denied
CENSUS.refuses: a score asserted
v1_2_evidence: no probability and no score anywhere in this task.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 says there is no score anywhere in this task

CENSUS.accepts: a domain word a source content statement carries
CENSUS.refuses: a domain word whose only supplied occurrence is inside a source metadata label
CENSUS.rationale: the operator's evidence-boundary decision (ADR-040); v1.2.0 predates it and never separates what a source reported from what it is called

CENSUS.accepts: a source named by its whole label, as provenance
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: the gate reads the whole label as a name before reading words
CENSUS.rationale: naming where a statement came from is always allowed, and a model told only that names are not evidence would stop attributing

CENSUS.accepts: domain vocabulary a source content statement carries
CENSUS.refuses: domain vocabulary no supplied statement carries at all
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 says prior knowledge is unavailable as factual support; the vocabulary list itself is class D
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^'[^']*' appears in no source content statement, compared under

CENSUS.accepts: such a quantity denied or named as unknown
CENSUS.refuses: a quantity no registered source measures, asserted
v1_2_evidence: Specifically, you may not assert anything about: how many people or organisations
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 lists at proposition level what may not be asserted; the term list itself is class D
CENSUS.refusal_signature: is not supportable by any registered source

CENSUS.accepts: a commercial term whose dimension the answer lists as supported and the packet carries
CENSUS.refuses: a commercial term asserting a dimension no eligible evidence supports
v1_2_evidence: Specifically, you may not assert anything about: how many people or organisations
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 forbids asserting these subjects at all, which is stricter than the gate
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^'[^']*' asserts [A-Z_]+, which no eligible evidence in this packet

CENSUS.accepts: a hypothesis record
CENSUS.refuses: wording that states a conclusion
v1_2_evidence: anything as high-confidence, validated, proven or significant.
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 forbids describing anything as validated, proven or high-confidence
CENSUS.refusal_signature: ^'[^']*' states a conclusion; this is a hypothesis record

CENSUS.accepts: an OBSERVED item that states one proposition, or denies alternatives together
CENSUS.refuses: an OBSERVED item that joins alternatives outside any denial
CENSUS.rationale: the gate evaluates no disjunction, so one classification over two alternatives fails closed; v1.2.0 predates the rule

CENSUS.accepts: a hypothesis, an unknown or a request kept as what it is
CENSUS.refuses: one promoted to a conclusion by certainty or validation wording
CENSUS.rationale: v1.2.0 forbids writing a hypothesis as an observation and never mentions certainty; the word list itself is class D
CENSUS.instruction: a hypothesis, an unknown and a request for evidence stay what they are: no adverb of certainty and no wording of confirmation turns one into a conclusion

CENSUS.accepts: an item that names a claim the packet does not support
CENSUS.refuses: an item that says the claim it names is established
CENSUS.rationale: rendered from the field's disposition; the predicate list that reads it is class D

CENSUS.accepts: one proposition a source content statement or a packet structural fact states itself
CENSUS.refuses: nothing beyond the vocabulary, number and disjunction rules: the gate evaluates no proposition's truth
CENSUS.rationale: a lexical match is necessary and never sufficient; the operator decided an OBSERVED statement is atomic and directly supported, which the gate cannot check and the prompt must say

CENSUS.accepts: a label that is not itself a gated term, read as a name
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: such a label is read as the term it spells
CENSUS.rationale: depends on what the registry calls a source, which no answer controls

CENSUS.accepts: the canonical name of a dimension listed as supported and carried by the packet
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: the name is read as a structural fact
v1_2_evidence: exactly these names, spelled exactly: PROBLEM_OR_NEED
CENSUS.rationale: the contract renders the dimension names, spelled exactly

CENSUS.accepts: an empty text or the sentinel UNKNOWN_NOT_SUPPORTED
CENSUS.refuses: nothing: such a text is not factual
v1_2_evidence: or the exact string UNKNOWN_NOT_SUPPORTED if they name none.
CENSUS.rationale: the contract renders the sentinel verbatim

CENSUS.accepts: nothing: a note, never a refusal
CENSUS.refuses: nothing
CENSUS.rationale: a record of an answer with nothing checkable in it, not a rule an answer follows

CENSUS.accepts: a word in any number its written rules fold
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: both sides of every comparison use one function
CENSUS.rationale: a normalizer rule; publishing it teaches which forms are compared and which are not

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: the verb forms a not-supported item may not use are matched verbatim
CENSUS.rationale: a word list; the proposition it enforces is rendered with the field's disposition

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: denials scope their clause, and a contrast after a denial re-asserts
CENSUS.rationale: how the gate reads grammar; publishing it would teach phrasing, and the propositions it protects are stated as propositions

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: the patterns that decide whether a shape was kept
CENSUS.rationale: patterns; the shapes they protect are rendered from the field policy

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: the lists the vocabulary rules above consult
CENSUS.rationale: a published list is a list of words to avoid, and a model that avoids the words has not stopped asserting the thing

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: labels are matched whole, longest first, never overlapping
CENSUS.rationale: a matching rule; publishing it would teach how to hide a word inside something shaped like a name

CENSUS.accepts: nothing on its own
CENSUS.refuses: nothing on its own: where a connective counts as joining alternatives
CENSUS.rationale: a boundary rule; the proposition it enforces is rendered as a proposition

COMPLIANCE_CASES.claim: a source name containing a domain word never yields an OBSERVED fact of that word
an atomic OBSERVED statement a source content statement establishes is allowed
an OBSERVED statement never joins alternatives
two statements are preferred to one joined statement
incomplete support gives HYPOTHESIS_TO_VALIDATE or UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE
a publisher's name may appear, whole, as provenance
a forbidden concept may appear as not supported or as unknown, never as observed
